Most developers test whether their app works.

I also wanted to see what happens when someone tries to break it. 💀

So, I built a Bit-Flip Attack Simulator for FileGuard.

The idea is simple:
🧪 Modify a file stored in the system.
🔍 Run a SHA-256 integrity check.
🚫 Block the download if the file's contents no longer match the original.

Basically, if someone messes with the file, FileGuard shouldn't just shrug and send it anyway.

Because “it downloaded successfully” doesn't necessarily mean “it's the right file.”

Next up: The infrastructure behind it. ☁️

#CyberSecurity #Python #SoftwareEngineering

Sending someone a file shouldn't require a leap of faith. 💀

You upload a file, share a link, and hope everything goes as planned.

But what happens if the file gets tampered with? And does “temporary” really mean temporary?

So I built FileGuard. 🔐

📁 Share files without creating an account
⏳ Files expire after 12 hours
🛡️ SHA-256 integrity checks to detect unexpected changes

The goal? Make file sharing a little less trust me, bro and a little more secure.

Tomorrow: What happens when I deliberately break a file to test the security. 👀
